The ground is stated in every note and is the edition's own printing, not an inference about it: one uninitialled apparatus, continuous across chapter heads in both the Pentateuch and the historical books, on ONE epoch throughout -- 2513 + 1491, 2944 + 1060, 2945 + 1059, 2947 + 1057, 2979 + 1025, 2980 + 1024, 2981 + 1023 all sum to the same number -- and one place where the edition names its chronologist, the note at Psalm 70:1 ending "3416 Usher", on that same epoch. column3: profiles.yaml `admissibility` -- the rule was STATED as a method test and ENFORCED as a disclosure test
column5: `rule` and `own_voice` read as a METHOD test: a value was inadmissible if the method behind it was excluded, and `modern-critical` said the exclusion held "whoever prints it". The corpus never enforced that and could not: what it actually applied, claim by claim, was a DISCLOSURE test, refusing a value only where its own source NAMED an excluded warrant -- Souvay's "inscription of Nabonidus", Sloet's "in conjunction with the data of profane history", Drum's "as Briggs surmises". A reviewer reading the profile and a reviewer reading the rulings got two different policies, and the second was discoverable only by reading code and notes. The narrowing was therefore silent, which is the defect: it could not be attacked on its merits because it was nowhere stated.
column6: `rule` states the disclosure test in terms: the basis test asks WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS THE VALUE RESTS ON, and refuses a value the work carrying it PRESENTS as resting on an excluded method. Four new leaves carry what that does and does not mean. `what_this_rule_does_not_do` says IT DOES NOT AUDIT PROVENANCE and gives the pair that makes the narrowness visible (Reid's 722 B.C. answered with, Sloet's 722-1 refused, both descending from the same eponym canon). `decision` records the maintainer's dated ruling and its reasoning -- a faithful method test would disqualify very nearly every absolute B.C. year in Old Testament history and leave the profile able to state almost nothing -- and says the narrowing is deliberate and that reversing it is a new profile id. `disclosure_is_read_not_inferred` requires the disclosure to be quoted from the source and forbids supplying it from this project's own knowledge. `corroboration_is_not_the_ground` distinguishes a sole warrant from an added confirmation and makes a claim taking the second reading show its primary ground. No machine part changed: the fifteen basis classes, `unstated: unresolved` and the Ussher reporting exception are untouched.
